content.value_statement: React Native test setup and failures can slow feature delivery. This skill provides focused Jest and React Native Testing Library patterns for creating, running, and debugging tests.
actual_capabilities: Sets up Jest scripts and React Native Testing Library dependencies.
Provides component test templates for rendered text and press events.
Provides hook and utility test templates.
Shows mocks for notifications, database clients, and navigation.
Explains commands for test runs, watch mode, coverage, snapshots, and selected files.
Offers troubleshooting guidance for timeouts, queries, mocks, and asynchronous tests.
limitations: Focuses on Jest and React Native Testing Library, not device-level end-to-end testing.
Does not configure a specific application or inspect its existing test setup.
Mock examples may need changes for a project’s aliases, libraries, and architecture.
Does not replace testing on physical devices or emulators.

use_cases.title: Add a component test
use_cases.description: Create a test for visible content and a button press in a React Native component.

use_cases.title: Debug a failing test
use_cases.description: Use the troubleshooting patterns to investigate timeouts, missing elements, mocks, and asynchronous behavior.

use_cases.title: Standardize test practices
use_cases.description: Apply the templates and best practices when introducing a consistent test approach to a mobile codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: create a component test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Jest test for my React Native Button component. Test that its label renders and its onPress handler runs once.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: test a hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Verify state changes in a custom hook.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a React Native Testing Library test for my useCounter hook. Test its initial count and increment behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: mock dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Isolate a screen from external services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me test a React Native screen that uses expo-router and a database client. Create focused Jest mocks and explain where to place them.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: diagnose asynchronous failure
prompt_templates.prompt: My React Native test times out while waiting for loaded content. Review this test flow and suggest a reliable waitFor or findBy strategy.

output_examples.input: Test a button that displays Save and calls onSave when pressed.
output: A component test that renders the Save label.
A press-event assertion that verifies onSave runs once.
A command that runs the selected test file.
A command that produces the Jest coverage report.

output_examples.input: A form should show an error for an invalid email address.
output: A test that enters an invalid email value.
An assertion that the Invalid email message is visible.

best_practices: Test user-visible behavior instead of internal implementation details.
Mock external dependencies to keep tests isolated and predictable.
Use asynchronous queries when the interface updates after an operation.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on implementation-specific state or private component methods.
Do not leave unresolved promises or timers in asynchronous tests.
Do not use broad mocks that hide important application behavior.

faq.question: Which testing tools does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Jest and React Native Testing Library for React Native applications.

faq.question: Can it help test custom hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a renderHook example that verifies state changes.

faq.question: Does it support mocking navigation?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows a Jest mock pattern for expo-router navigation methods.

faq.question: How can I run one test file?
faq.answer: Use Jest with the target test filename after the test command.

faq.question: How can I investigate a missing element?
faq.answer: Inspect rendered output with screen.debug and use appropriate query methods.

faq.question: Does this skill perform device end-to-end tests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on local Jest tests rather than emulator or physical-device testing.
